title: Each render has its own Effect

slides.say: Think of use effect as attaching behavior to one render’s output. Each render has its own Effect.
Mentally substitute the values. The first render’s Effect connects to general, with dependencies general.

slides.text: Re-render with ["general"] again? React ignores that render’s Effect. It is never called.
slides.say: Re-render with the same room? React compares the dependencies, sees they match, and ignores that render’s Effect completely.

slides.text: roomId becomes "travel": cleanup from render 1 runs, then render 3’s Effect.
slides.say: When room id becomes travel, React runs the cleanup from the last Effect that ran, disconnecting general, then runs the new render’s Effect.
